source_text:
Ἀλλ’ ὅγε ψευδοπροφήτης ἐν παρεκστάσει· ᾧ ἕπεται ἄδεια καὶ ἀφοβία· ἀρχόμενος μὲν ἐξ ἑκουσίου ἀμαθίας, καταστρέφων δὲ εἰς ἀκούσιον μανίαν ψυχῆς, ὡς προείρηται. τοῦτον δὲ τὸν τρόπον, οὔ τέ τινα τῶν κατὰ τὴν παλαιὰν, οὔτε τῶν κατὰ τὴν καινὴν πνευματοφορηθέντα προφήτην δεῖξαι δυνήσονται· ᵃοὔτε Ἄγαβον· οὔτε Ἰούδαν· οὔτε Σίλαν· οὔτε τὰς Φιλίππου θυγατέρας· οὔτε τὴν ἐν Φιλαδελφείᾳ Ἀμμίαν· οὔτε Κοδράτον· οὔτε γε δή τινας ἄλλους μηδὲν αὐτοῖς προσήκοντας καυχήσονται. αὖθις δὲ μετὰ βραχέα, ταῦτα φησίν·
Εἰ γὰρ μετὰ Κοδράτον καὶ τὴν ἐν Φιλαδελφείᾳ Ἀμμίαν, ὥς φασιν, αἱ περὶ Μοντανὸν διεδέξαντο γυναῖκες τὸ προφητικὸν χάρισμα, τοὺς ἀπὸ Μοντανοῦ καὶ τῶν γυναικῶν τίνες παρ’ αὐτοῖς διεδέξαντο, δειξάτωσαν· δεῖν γὰρ εἶναι τὸ προφητικὸν χάρισμα ἐν πάσῃ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ μέχρι τῆς τελείας παρουσίας ὁ ἀπόστολος ἀξιοῖ· ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἂν ἔχοιεν δεῖξαι τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατον ἤδη που τοῦτο ἔτος ἀπὸ τῆς Μαξιμίλλης τελευτῆς.
thought_title: The false prophet's ecstasy and the unprovable succession
orientation: The author is quoting from a Montanist writing against Miltiades, then continues his own argument that no genuine prophet, old or new, can be shown to have prophesied in ecstasy, and that the Montanists cannot show successors to Montanus and the women.
pass_a_gloss: But the false prophet is in ecstasy; to whom follows recklessness and fearlessness; beginning indeed from voluntary ignorance, but ending in involuntary madness of soul, as has been said before. And in this manner, they will not be able to show any prophet of those according to the old covenant, nor of those according to the new covenant, who was borne by the spirit; neither Agabus; nor Judas; nor Silas; nor the daughters of Philip; nor Ammia in Philadelphia; nor Quadratus; nor indeed will they boast of any others who have nothing to do with them. And again after a little, he says these things: For if after Quadratus and Ammia in Philadelphia, as they say, the women around Montanus succeeded to the prophetic spiritual gift, let them show who among them succeeded to those from Montanus and the women; for the apostle deems it necessary that the prophetic spiritual gift be in the whole church until the final coming; but they would not be able to show, this being already the fourteenth year, I suppose, from the death of Maximilla.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'ecstasy' for παρέκστασις, and the prepositional phrase keeps the state in which the false prophet operates.
The participle conveys passive inspiration by the spirit, matching the author's contrast between genuine prophets and the false prophet's ecstasy.
The glossary requires 'spiritual gift' for χάρισμα, and the adjective 'prophetic' is kept to preserve the full phrase.
The adjective τελείας here means 'final' or 'complete', referring to the eschatological coming of Christ, not a 'perfect' coming.

choices.english: this being already the fourteenth year, I suppose
choices.why: The particle που softens the assertion, so 'I suppose' captures the author's hedging tone; the number is kept literal.
rejected: this is now the fourteenth year

pass_b_english: But the false prophet speaks in ecstasy, and with ecstasy come recklessness and fearlessness. He begins with willful ignorance and ends, as I said before, in involuntary madness of soul. They will not be able to show that any prophet of the old covenant or the new was borne by the Spirit in this way. Not Agabus, not Judas, not Silas, not Philip's daughters, not Ammia in Philadelphia, not Quadratus. Nor will they boast of any others who have nothing to do with them.
Then a little later the same author says this:

"For if, as they claim, the women around Montanus succeeded to the prophetic spiritual gift after Quadratus and Ammia in Philadelphia, let them show who among them succeeded to those from Montanus and the women. The apostle insists that the prophetic spiritual gift must remain in the whole church until the final coming. But they could not show anyone, this being already the fourteenth year, I suppose, since Maximilla's death."

problems.quote: For if, as they claim, the women around Montanus succeeded to the prophetic spiritual gift after Quadratus and Ammia in Philadelphia, let them show who among them succeeded to those from Montanus and the women.
problems.why: Eusebius introduces with 'Then a little later he says this' but 'he' refers to anonymous author; reader may think new speaker.

problems.quote: He even roused two other women
problems.why: Maximilla and Priscilla introduced vaguely, then referenced as 'the women' without naming them again.
problems.fix: Name Maximilla and Priscilla at first mention and clarify later references.

problems.quote: Then a little later he says this:
problems.why: 'He' again ambiguous; unclear if same source as previous section.

edits.old: Then a little later he says this:
edits.new: Then a little later the same author says this:

fixed: The 'he' in 'Then a little later he says this' refers to the anonymous author of the work against Asterius Urbanus, not a new speaker; clarified as 'the same author'.
The glossary problem about Maximilla and Priscilla is not present in this section; no edit needed.
The speaker problem is the same as the first; the 'he' is the anonymous author, now clarified.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker attribution for the quoted passage, made the list of prophets easier to follow, and smoothed the final sentence about the fourteenth year so the argument lands clearly.
